newsitem.title: INDIA: Star TV channel goes local to woo India.
newsitem.headline: Star TV channel goes local to woo India.

text.p: An English-language satellite channel broadcast by media baron Rupert Murdoch's Star Television will air Hindi programmes in India at prime time, company executives said on Thursday.
"My mandate has been to Indianise Star Plus," said Rathikant Basu, a former chief of India's state-run Doordarshan television lured away by Murdoch, whose Newscorp owns the Hong Kong-based Star TV.
"Only those programmes that meet with cultural and other sensibilities will be on Star Plus," said Basu, Star TV's new chief executive officer for India.
Last year a grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, spiritual father of independent India, sued Star TV over an insulting remark on Gandhi made by a guest on a talk show.
A key part of Star Plus's new line-up would be prime-time news bulletins in Hindi and English focused on India.
Basu said Star Plus would offer Hindi programmes and dubbed versions in Hindi of soap serials like "The Bold and the Beautiful" and "Baywatch."

With new programmes focused on India, advertising was expected to look up, Star officials said. Advertising revenue is expected to grow to $10-12 million in 1996/97 (July-June), up from $9.0 million in 1995/96.
Gene Swinstead, Star TV's managing director in India, said the Indianisation of Star Plus was part of a strategy by the channel across Asia to offer more local programming.
"We have pursued a localisation policy vigorously since we moved to India," Swinstead said.
Basu said cable television had penetrated only around one quarter of India's 50 million households with television sets, and Star TV had its limitations.

"I must make the point clear that Doordarshan today has no competition in programming," said Basu, who has been credited with turning a dull state television station into a lively and financially successful broadcaster.
